title: Q-FULLSTACK-second-tenant: the second-tenant seed gets its own repository and a public front end
body:
**Owner:** executor
**Trigger:** executor tick, driver order
**Done check:** cmd:python3 -m foundation fullstack --probe second-tenant
**Status:** open

FULLSTACK-1: every system deploys its repository, its back end and a public web front end. The seed `second-tenant` has a live back end (ultrastable-seed-second-tenant) and nothing else: its code sits in instances/second-tenant in the core repository and deploy/deploy-seed.mjs binds PUBLIC_HEALTH_ONLY=1, so it serves /health only. Give it its own repository through doctrine/tenant-repos.json (the same route as the other tenants), serve a public page from its Worker (seed/worker/src/visibility.js keeps the owner routes closed; the public page shows what the system is and what it did), then set `repo` and `frontend` for it in doctrine/full-stack.json and remove its `gaps`. Paths: doctrine/full-stack.json, doctrine/tenant-repos.json, deploy/deploy-seed.mjs, seed/worker/src/visibility.js, seed/worker/src/index.js.

size: M

**Closing probe:** python3 -m foundation fullstack --probe second-tenant passes and python3 -m foundation fullstack --live shows its front end live
